pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The venue manager’s proposal
paragraphs: The venue manager proposes digital-first payments to simplify checkout and reconciliation and reduce cash handling. They are willing to discuss a trial and a fallback when the usual payment route is unavailable.
No trial has yet established savings or faster service. Equipment costs and transaction fees are still unknown, so the expected benefits remain aims rather than measured results.

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The customer representative’s concern
paragraphs: The customer representative wants people to be able to pay without a working device, a particular account or a reliable connection. A dead battery or a temporary outage can prevent a customer from using the normal digital route.

They also want clear information about fees, privacy and a usable fallback. Their concern is whether a customer can complete a purchase when digital payment fails, not whether every customer should always pay in cash.

pages.title: Read and explain the evidence

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: An ordinary user loses digital access. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I wanted to add an experience to the payment-policy discussion. I normally pay by card, but last week my phone battery died while I was out. At the next place, the payment connection also stopped working for a while. I had some cash with me, but their digital-only process didn’t allow it, so I couldn’t complete the purchase then. I’m not saying that one incident proves digital payment is always unreliable. It does show that temporary loss of access can affect people who usually use it comfortably. Could your recommendation say what happens in that situation, including how staff explain the fallback without embarrassing the customer? I’d also want to know whether a transaction fee changes between the normal process and the fallback. A policy can aim for convenience while still making a specific plan for the moment the convenient route fails

items.answer: The speaker’s phone battery died and the venue’s payment connection stopped working

items.answer: The fallback should address staff explanation without embarrassment and any different transaction fee

items.prompt: What is the intended function of pooling those payments?

items.prompt: Does giving a payment to one worker guarantee that worker receives it all?
items.hint: Listen to the explanation after the interview

items.prompt: Recommend a tipping policy that considers both customers and workers
